Wafer
WAY-fer
noun
“Wafer” comes through Old French waufre from a Germanic root (kin to waffle and weave), naming a thin cake baked on a flat iron. In the KJV it renders Hebrew raqiq, a thin unleavened cake of the offerings.

Biblical Definition

In the KJV a wafer is a thin flat cake of unleavened bread, used in the holy offerings and likened to the manna. The modern reader hears “wafer” and may think of a communion-host of the Roman altar, or a light biscuit; the AV means a plain, thin, leaven-free cake, Hebrew raqiq, baked without yeast for the service of God. It stands among the priestly breads. At the consecration of Aaron the LORD commanded “unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened tempered with oil, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil: of wheaten flour shalt thou make them” (Exo 29:2); and Moses took from the basket “one unleavened cake, and a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer” and laid them on the fat of the offering (Lev 8:26). At the close of the Nazarite’s vow the priest took “one unleavened wafer” and put it upon his hands (Num 6:19). The wafer, then, is a bread of dedication, thin and pure, anointed with oil — a fit figure of a life offered wholly to God. And when Israel first gathered the manna, that bread from heaven, they found its taste “like wafers made with honey” (Exo 16:31): the daily gift of God as sweet as the holy cake of His altar. The reader should see in the wafer no wafer-god, but a simple, sincere, unleavened bread of offering.

Webster 1828 Definition

A thin unleavened cake of the offerings, likened to the manna — not the wafer-host of Rome.

WAFER, a thin flat cake of unleavened bread, used in the holy offerings.

From Old French waufre, of Germanic root, kin to waffle and weave.

In the KJV it renders Hebrew raqiq, a thin leaven-free cake anointed with oil.

Used at Aaron’s consecration and the Nazarite’s offering (Exo 29:2; Num 6:19).

The manna tasted “like wafers made with honey” (Exo 16:31).

Key Scripture

Exo 16:31 — "And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey."

Exo 29:2 — "And unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened tempered with oil, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil: of wheaten flour shalt thou make them."

Lev 8:26 — "And out of the basket of unleavened bread, that was before the LORD, he took one unleavened cake, and a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, and put them on the fat, and upon the right shoulder:"

Num 6:19 — "And the priest shall take the sodden shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened cake out of the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put them upon the hands of the Nazarite, after the hair of his separation is shaven:"

Modern Corruption

Not a live postmodern redefinition but a caution: the KJV wafer is a bread of offering, not the consecrated host of the Roman Mass.

expand to see more

The word “wafer” now carries an association the KJV never intended: to many ears it means the round wafer of the Roman Mass, held to be transubstantiated into the body of Christ. The Authorized Version’s wafer is nothing of the kind. It is a thin unleavened cake of the Levitical offerings, a piece of ordinary wheaten dough baked without yeast and anointed with oil. A reader who imports the Mass into Exo 29:2 or Num 6:19 reads his own age’s error back into Moses.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the meaning of the unleavened wafer itself: a bread of dedication, thin, pure, and free of the leaven that puffs and sours. Such cakes were laid on the altar at the making of a priest and set in the hand of the Nazarite whose vow was fulfilled — tokens of a life set apart and offered whole to God, without the leaven of corruption. And the manna, God’s own bread from heaven, tasted like wafers made with honey: His daily provision as pure and sweet as the bread of His sanctuary. Let the wafer preach dedication and sincerity, not a wafer to be adored.
